title: OIDC SSO RS256/JWKS verifier spike
story: As a carrier IT admin I want the platform to verify my IdP ID tokens so that dev tokens can be retired.
requirements: Security: no alg confusion, fail closed
acceptance: src/core/oidc.mjs exports createOidcVerifier({issuer, audience, jwks, clockSkewSec, now}) where jwks is a port {getKeys(){Promise<JWK[]>}, optional refresh}; verify(token) resolves claims or throws a typed error with a stable code. Uses only node:crypto (createPublicKey with format jwk, verify RSASSA-PKCS1-v1_5 SHA-256).

tests/unit/core/spikes/oidc.test.mjs (run with node --test) passes and covers: valid token; wrong iss; wrong aud (string and array aud); expired exp; future nbf; clock skew boundary; unknown kid triggers one JWKS refresh then succeeds (rotation) and fails if still unknown; tampered payload/signature; alg=none rejected; HS256 token signed with the RSA public key as HMAC secret rejected (key confusion); missing kid; malformed token segments; only RS256 accepted.
Tests use a locally generated RSA keypair and a fake JWKS port; no network, no fixtures with real keys or secrets.
auth.mjs, server.mjs, store.mjs and dev-token behaviour untouched (git diff clean); module is not imported anywhere in src/.

architecture/spikes/oidc-sso.md covers: discovery and JWKS fetch/caching/refresh rate limit design, claim-to-tenant/role mapping proposal, nonce/state out of scope notes, threat table (alg confusion, kid injection, replay, JWKS poisoning/SSRF), Sprint 6 wiring plan after security review, and a documented live-check command for the orchestrator (not under tests/).
brief: Design plus proof, not wiring. Implement base64url decode manually (Buffer.from(s,'base64url')), parse header/payload JSON defensively (reject non-objects, size cap ~8KB). Pipeline: split in 3 segments; header.alg must be exactly 'RS256' (reject none, HS*, anything else BEFORE touching keys); header.typ optional; require kid; find key in jwks.getKeys() where kty==='RSA', kid matches, and (use absent or 'sig'); if kid unknown call jwks.refresh() at most once per verify (and rate-limit refreshes via a minimum interval using injected now) then retry. Build the key with createPublicKey({key: jwk, format:'jwk'}) and crypto.verify('sha256', data, key, sig). Never use the token to pick a key type or secret. Then validate iss strict equality, aud (string or array includes), exp required and > now - skew, nbf <= now + skew, iat sanity optional. Errors: class OidcError with code (e.g. bad_token, bad_alg, unknown_kid, bad_signature, bad_iss, bad_aud, expired, not_yet_valid) and no token contents in messages (logs redact). Also export a fake-friendly createStaticJwks(keys) helper for tests. Tests: generate keys with generateKeyPairSync('rsa',{modulusLength:2048}), export jwk via publicKey.export({format:'jwk'}), sign with crypto.sign. HS256 confusion: craft header alg HS256 and HMAC-sign with the PEM public key and assert bad_alg. The doc needs a threat table informed by architecture/threat-model.md. Synthetic issuer such as https://idp.example.test only.

verdicts.reason: All criteria met; 19/19 oidc tests pass, no src imports, auth/server/store untouched, regression gate 0 fail matches baseline
